title: fix(verify): the rapid law reads the stock's top under the rapid, not its highest point
body:
**Merged main after #971/#1064/#957** (#1077, this PR's parent, is merged). The local merge had no textual conflict; I re-read both verify sites in `generate.rs` by hand, and the re-reading still runs at both before `acquit_by_prior`, on world facets and local facets respectively. Two decisions came out of the merge:
- **Band stack (#957/#993):** the re-reading is never narrower than the laws read the stack.
  - The shank is read at the **stated** shank radius. A drawn neck's bands are never wider than it.
  - Above the shank, it reads `max(holder, shank)`, `BodyBands`' bound there.
  - Raw numbers are checked before the `max`, because `f64::max` drops a NaN; a unit test caught this.
- **Excess (#1064):** `model_excess` grows every band's disc and raises every top by the excess, so a dive that clears the meshed material by less than the excess stays convicted. A non-finite excess keeps the conviction. Pinned by `a_coarse_models_excess_is_read_up_and_sideways`.
- **Third review (#1056 guard):** a from-model stock reads its chord only through its source model. `model_fidelity::stock_fidelity_known(setup)` decides whether the stock is passed to the re-reading:
  - box, cylinder or no stock: known;
  - from-model: known only while its source model stands (no record means exact);
  - otherwise both sites pass no stock, and every conviction stands.

  A `// #1056` note marks the guard: once #1127 lands, it reads the stock's own chord. The fixtures now keep the casting in the tree, marked raw stock only (`SetStockSourceOnly`, #1094), with the part beside it. Pinned by `a_coarse_stock_whose_source_is_gone_is_never_acquitted` (fails with the guard off) and `a_coarse_stock_whose_source_stands_reads_its_excess`.
- **Fourth review (proof of the source, option (a)):** the named source counts only if its current local facets are the stock's own: the same `Arc`, or the same count with every coordinate equal bit for bit. An exact model imported under a deleted coarse casting's name is therefore not the source. Placement is not compared: the chord belongs to the mesh, and `MoveModel` carries the copy with the source. `UpdateModel` updates the copy and the fidelity record together. There is no model-rename command. I chose (a) over a stored fingerprint (b): it needs no schema or project-file field, it is an exact equality rather than a hash, and `stock_print` stays the only fingerprint. Pinned by `an_exact_model_imported_under_the_old_name_proves_nothing` and `the_guard_follows_the_mesh_not_the_name`; both fail with a name-only guard.
- **Also fixed:** `crates/app/src/operation/rotary_law_tests.rs` gains `neck: None`. Main's app lib tests do not compile since #1064 added that `Cutter` literal and #957 added the field.

## What changed

Law (d) (#96, `RapidInStock`) caps every column at `stock_top_z`, the stock's highest point. On a stepped "from model" or carried stock, a Bore's entry dive to just above the low part was convicted as if the boss stood there too, and the post was blocked for a legal program.

- **`crates/sim/src/verify/stock_top.rs` (new): `verify::acquit_by_stock_top`.** It works like `acquit_by_prior`: it re-reads the convictions the column law gave **upright vertical rapids down**, in column modes only (radial, revolved and rotary are excluded), and it can only **remove** a conviction. A dive is acquitted only when every band of the tool stack ends above the highest vertex of every stock or part facet whose plan comes within that band's disc:
  - the flute at its full radius (no `- gouge_tol`, no ball lift), from the tip;
  - the shank, from the flute's top;
  - the holder, from the shank's top.

  On a closed mesh this is an exact upper bound on the material in the disc, and slopes read high. It fails closed: a non-finite stack number, or a flute disc that meets no facet, leaves the conviction standing.
- **Closed-shell gate (review fix, `crates/sim/src/verify/stock_top_shell.rs`).** The bound holds only on a closed surface, so a solid that fails this gate keeps the conviction. To pass, a solid must:
  - be non-empty, with every vertex finite;
  - have no facet that is degenerate in 3-D;
  - use every undirected edge (endpoints matched exactly) in **exactly two facets, once in each direction**;
  - form one edge-connected shell;
  - have a positive signed volume.

  Open shells, non-manifold or duplicated edges, inside-out or split solids all keep the conviction. The check runs once per solid per operation, in O(F) with an edge hash map, never per rapid. It does not test self-intersection: the ray argument behind the bound holds for any closed surface, self-intersecting or not (see the decision file).
- **`crates/app/src/operation/stock_top_law.rs` (new)** is the wiring. The solids are #1077's `judged_stock` (the setup's or carried stock, or the stock itself for a stock-sourced Bore/Thread) plus the op's own material. With no judged stock (the op's region stood in for it), every conviction stands. It is called at both `VerifyContext` sites in `generate.rs` (+6 lines net), before `acquit_by_prior`. The 3+2 site passes the plane's local facets.
- The column law itself (`rapids.rs`, `Rest::surface_before`) is unchanged, so lateral rapids, the posed and radial readings and the solid law keep their verdicts. Thread's descent is a vertical rapid and goes through the same re-reading.

## Readings

The first reproduction used stock only, with the casting deleted. Since #1094 was fixed (PR #1097), the fixtures keep the casting in the tree, marked raw stock only. The casting is solid to Z 20 over a 16 mm hole, with a boss to Z 30 at x 18..28. Before the fix, the part-sourced Bore's dive to Z 22 gave `[RapidInStock { at: 0 }]`. I confirmed this again after the fix by disabling the wiring: the pin fails. After the fix it is silent and the program posts, for the part-sourced and the stock-sourced Bore alike.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/stepped_stock_rapid.rs` (new suite, 8 tests, each run for a part-sourced and a stock-sourced Bore):
  - `a_dive_over_the_low_part_of_a_stepped_stock_passes_and_posts`
  - `the_same_dive_with_the_boss_under_it_is_convicted`: convicted, and the post is blocked by the rapid law.
  - `a_boss_reaching_into_the_tool_footprint_is_convicted`: the boss edge is 1.5 mm beside the dive's centre, under the 4 mm rim.
  - `a_coarse_stock_whose_source_is_gone_is_never_acquitted` and `a_coarse_stock_whose_source_stands_reads_its_excess` (#1056 guard).
  - `an_open_stock_mesh_proves_nothing_and_the_dive_stays_convicted`: the review's case (the boss over the hole without its top facets) is convicted and the post is blocked. It fails with the gate off.
- `sim::verify::stock_top::tests` (13 tests): the low step of a closed single-shell stepped stock is acquitted; a boss over the dive, or under the rim only, stands; a holder band over the boss on a stubby tool stands; a part under the dive counts; an open shell, a non-manifold or duplicated edge, a degenerate facet, an inside-out or split solid, an empty solid and a non-finite vertex all keep the conviction; a coarse model's excess is read up and sideways; posed and lateral dives and the radial, revolved and rotary modes are never re-read.

## How tested

All green:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test stepped_stock_rapid --test ladder_entry_height --test operations --test golden_cl --test coarse_laws --test coarse_contain --test stock_source_verdict --test model_fidelity` | 8 / 4 / 117 (6 ignored) / 25 / 6 (before main's #1074 wording change; see below) / 1 / 22 / 9 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --lib verify` | 27 passed |
| sim `vertical_rapids` / `sideways_rapids` / `posed_rapids` / `radial_rapids` / `coarse_collision` / `model_excess` | 16 / 3 / 5 / 15 / 5 / 5 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` | on `ae25d334` (final head): sim, motion and ui green; app green except 4 `coarse_laws` tests that expect the old refusal text "larger budget". Main's #1074 changed that text to "larger STEP facet budget"; this is main's break, tracked as #1175, and the file is untouched by this PR. 17.6 min |

No goldens moved, and the existing rapid-law pins (`ladder_entry_height`, the #96 pins) are unchanged.

## Not exercised

- No end-to-end test of a 3+2 (tilted) Bore on a stepped stock, and none of Thread. Both go through the same sim reading, which is unit-pinned.
- No test of a carried stock with a boss. Its facets are the judged stock, so it goes through the same path.
- Imported meshes with T-junctions or vertices that are not welded bit for bit are not closed by this rule, so they keep the flat-cap verdict. That is a refusal, never a pass.
- A from-model stock whose source is gone is never acquitted (the #1056 guard), even when it is in fact exact.
- The excess is the op's own model excess, applied to the stock and part solids alike. A stock mesh coarser than its source carries no excess of its own (nor does the column law).
- Lateral rapids over a stepped stock still read the flat cap. They over-report and hide nothing (#1095).
- A model that is neither the op's source nor inside the stock (a second part poking up through a low step) is not among the solids. The flat cap did not read it there either.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1091-rapid-law-local-top.md`.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: The rapid-in-stock law reads the stock's top under a vertical dive instead of its highest point, so a legal entry dive over the low part of a stepped (from-model or carried) stock no longer blocks the post. A dive into the boss, or with the boss under the tool's rim or stack, is still refused.

Fixes #1091
